notes:
## Sounds Like, from a selection

- Select a word in a block's text and a **Sounds Like** button pops up under it. Click it and Sounds like opens with the word already filled in, so all that's left is typing how it should sound.
- It shows **Sounds Like ✓** for a word that already has a pronunciation. Alt+Shift+P still works too.

## Screen readers

- Scribecue's messages, such as "Block #3 marked", are now read out by screen readers, with key symbols said as words.
- The block list is a list a screen reader can move through: each block is read with its number, start, length and text, and the selected one is marked.
- The buttons and indicators under the video say what they do, and whether they're on, and the clock says it copies the timecode.
- A reading too long for its block now says "too long", and gets a ⚠ in the list, not only red.
- Faint grey text is a little lighter, so it's easier to read.

## Also

- **Transcribe** and **Write** are now a sliding switch at the top left. Click either side, or the side that's on, to switch.

## Remove all data

- The offline window is now **Offline and storage**, opened from the bottom right, in the Docker version too. It ends with **Remove all data**, which clears everything Scribecue keeps in this browser: unsaved blocks, settings and shortcuts, AI keys, downloaded Piper voices and Whisper, and its offline copy.
- It warns you first, says how many unsaved blocks would be lost, and offers to save the project. Your project files, and anything in Docker, stay as they are. Afterwards Scribecue opens as if for the first time.

## Fix

- Browsers built on the same engine as Chrome, such as Brave, Opera, Vivaldi and Arc, no longer get the notice about features that may not work, unless something really is missing. Scribecue now checks what your browser can do, rather than going by its name, and only lists what it lacks.

## Working offline

- **offline ready** in the bottom right opens a checklist of what this browser has for working without a connection: Scribecue itself, the guides, your Piper voices and Whisper, and whether the browser will keep them. Anything missing has a button to get it.
- While you're offline, the bottom right says **offline**. AI help says when an online provider can't be reached, and points to Ollama, which works offline. Online voices are greyed out.
- Scribecue now asks the browser to keep its storage, so it's less likely to be cleared when space runs low.

## Guides inside Scribecue

- The README and the transcribing, AI and install guides now open inside Scribecue, with their screenshots, and work offline. **Guides** in the shortcuts overlay (press ?) opens them, and links to them anywhere in Scribecue open there too.

## Phones, tablets and old browsers

- On a phone or tablet, Scribecue now says it needs a computer, rather than opening an editor that can't be used there.
- Browsers from before 2022, too old to run Scribecue, now say so instead of showing a blank page.

## Autosave

- Autosave is now always on wherever it works. The status next to the project name only shows what it's doing; click it when it says **autosave paused** or **autosave failed** to carry on. If you'd turned autosave off, it's back on.
- Autosave only runs in browsers that can save straight back to a file, which are Chrome and Edge. In Firefox and Safari, the notice when Scribecue opens now says autosave isn't available there.

## Fix

- The autosave status now sits right after the project and video names at the top, where it's easy to find, instead of over by the buttons on the right.

## Autosave

- Once a project has a file, Scribecue now saves your changes to it as you work, a couple of seconds after you stop. **autosaved** next to the project name says it's done.
- After a reload, the browser asks before Scribecue may save to the file again, so the status says **autosave paused**. Click it, or press Ctrl/Cmd+S, and it carries on. Opening a project asks straight away.
- Click **autosaved** to turn autosave off, and **autosave off** to turn it back on. The file always has your latest changes, so save a copy with Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+S before a big change if you might want the old version.
- Autosave needs Chrome or Edge. In other browsers, the reminder to save still helps.

## Speech to text

- **Spelling:** Whisper writes American spelling, and the speech to text panel can now change it to British and Canadian spelling as the text arrives: colour, grey, centre, travelled, catalogue and the like. It starts on whichever suits your browser's language.
- The panel links to the new [transcribing guide](https://github.com/kyle95wm/Scribecue/blob/main/TRANSCRIBING.md), which covers everything about transcribing, from choosing the description track to fixing what Whisper gets wrong.

## A reminder to save

- Until you save a project, your work is only kept in the browser. After 20 minutes of unsaved work, a note now asks you to save it. **Later** asks again in half an hour.

## Fix

- **Install app** in the bottom right now only shows when your browser can install Scribecue. It used to show everywhere, including when Scribecue was already installed and in the Docker version, where clicking it did nothing.

## Firefox

- In Firefox, the notice when Scribecue opens now also says what doesn't work well there: a file's description track can stutter or cut out, and speech to text can interrupt the video's sound. If you turned the notice off, it shows once more with the new list.
- The speech to text panel says so too. Both work best in Chrome or Edge.

## Fixes

- With speech to text on, marking a few blocks could stop the video's sound altogether in Firefox. Each block's audio is now read without holding on to the browser's audio decoders.
- A file's description track, when it plays alongside the video, no longer stutters or cuts out briefly in Firefox. It stays in step with fewer, gentler adjustments.
- The Whisper container leaves half your processor for the browser, so playback stays smooth while a block is transcribed. It's just as fast.

## Speech to text, for transcribing

- In Transcribe mode, **Whisper** can type each line for you. You still time every block by holding H; when you let go, Whisper listens to the block's audio and fills in what the narrator said, ready to check. If you start typing first, it leaves the block to you.
- Click **STT** under the video, or press Alt+Shift+H, to set it up. In the web version, Whisper is a one-time 166 MB download into your browser, and then it works offline. With Docker, add the new Whisper container, which is more accurate (see [INSTALL.md](https://github.com/kyle95wm/Scribecue/blob/main/INSTALL.md#speech-to-text-whisper)).
- **Transcribe empty blocks** fills in every block with no text yet, in one go. Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes it.
- Alt+Shift+T transcribes the selected block again, such as after you change its timing.
- It all runs on your computer: the audio is never uploaded. Whisper understands English, and it hears everything in a block, so choose the description track with T if your file has one.

## Only models that work, in AI help

- **Load models** in AI help's settings now only lists models that can look at your frames and write a description. Ones that couldn't help, such as models that only handle text, make pictures, speak, or work in slow batches, are left out, for every provider.
- For Ollama, models you've downloaded that can't see images aren't listed. If none can, the settings say which one to download.

## The loop, when you need it

- The loop to work in now shows after setup, for the mode you picked, instead of inside the guided tour. The first time you switch to the other mode, its loop shows too.
- **Show the loop** in the shortcuts overlay (press ?) brings it back any time.

## Also

- Setup's text to speech step now has **Don't read notes in [square brackets]**.
- AI help has a new guide, [AI.md](https://github.com/kyle95wm/Scribecue/blob/main/AI.md): connecting each provider, which models to use, including Ollama models for each size of computer, and getting the best descriptions. AI help's settings link to it.
- Drafts with Ollama keep more room for frames and the script around the block, so long requests aren't cut short.

## What's new, after every update

- When Scribecue updates, a window like this one now lists everything that changed since the version you were on, newest first.
- Click the version number in the bottom right to see this release's notes again.

## Piper voices in setup

- In the web version, setup now offers to download a natural-sounding Piper voice, with the voices in your language first and the download size. It downloads in the background when you finish, and it's chosen once it's ready.
- Piper is now marked as recommended, in setup and the text to speech panel: its voices sound natural, give exact reading lengths, and can be exported as a description track.

## The tour comes first, and shows you the loop

- On a first visit, the guided tour now comes first, and the setup follows when it ends, whether you finish it or skip it with Esc. Setup at the top still runs just the setup, and the tour is in the shortcuts overlay (press ?).
- The tour now ends with the loop to work in for your mode: finding a gap, writing and hearing a description in Write mode, or playing, marking and typing each line in Transcribe mode. It uses your own keys if you've changed them.
- Exports are now described as "to hand off".

## Change your keyboard shortcuts

- Press **?** and click **Change shortcuts** to give any editor action the keys you like. Click **Add** and press the keys; if they already belong to another action, Scribecue asks before moving them. Click a key to take it off, and **Reset** puts an action back.
- **Export** saves your shortcuts as a file and **Import** loads one, so a team can share a layout.
- The shortcuts overlay and the player buttons' tooltips show the keys you're using.
- Keys with Ctrl/Cmd, keys used while typing, and ? / [ ] + − Esc stay as they are.

## A guided tour

- A one-minute tour now lights up each part of Scribecue in turn and explains it: the two modes, the video and timeline, the block editor and list, text to speech, AI help, projects and exports, privacy, and where the shortcuts are.
- Setup offers it at the end, and **Take the tour** in the shortcuts overlay (press ?) shows it again. Use → and ← to step through, and Esc to stop.

## Also new

- A small GitHub mark in the bottom right opens Scribecue's page on GitHub: the source, releases and a place to report problems.
- Setting Scribecue up yourself with Docker now has its own guide, [INSTALL.md](https://github.com/kyle95wm/Scribecue/blob/main/INSTALL.md), so the README is just about using it.

## A tidier header

- **Open** is now one button for everything: a project, a script (SRT or VTT), or a video or audio file, and you can pick several at once, such as a project and its video. Each opens as the right thing. Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+O still opens only video or audio.
- **Export** is now a small menu: the script as SRT (Ctrl/Cmd+E), the script as WebVTT (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+E), and in Write mode the description track (WAV).
- Every keyboard shortcut is unchanged.

## Clear the blocks, keep the video

- **New** now asks how you want to start again. **Clear the blocks** removes every block and keeps the video, the project file and your notes, ready to write from scratch on the same video. **New project** clears everything and closes the video, as before.
- Either way, Ctrl/Cmd+Z brings the blocks back.

Tip: to swap in a different script, just open it with Ctrl/Cmd+O. That replaces the blocks and keeps the video.

## The web version updates without asking

- No more "reload" prompt for every release. A new version is used as you open Scribecue, before you've started anything.
- If one arrives while you're working, nothing interrupts you: the version number in the bottom right shows **update ready**. Click it to update then, or it's used the next time you open Scribecue.
- Your blocks, notes and settings are kept either way.

This release itself still arrives with one last reload prompt, because the previous version is the one that spots it. From now on, updates happen on their own.

## Headroom in the exported description track

- The exported description track is no longer at full scale. Every reading now peaks at −8 dBFS, so blocks are evenly matched and there's headroom for processing and mastering.
- Readings that run into the next block overlap in the file, but never take it past −6 dBFS.

## Fix: exporting a long description track in the web version

- In the web version, exporting a description track, or other long jobs such as Fit speeds to timings, with a Piper voice could stop with "Couldn't export the description track: Aborted()." This came in with 0.22.0 and happened after about 80 blocks. Long exports now finish.

The Docker version wasn't affected. Running it? Update as usual: `git pull`, then `docker compose up -d --build`.

## A more realistic voice test

- **Test** in the text to speech panel now reads a short passage of the kind of audio description you'd hear in a drama, instead of one short line, so you can judge a voice's pace, pauses and tone on what it will actually read. **Try it** reads the same passage when no block is selected.

## Previous block works from the playhead

- **Alt+Shift+←** now goes back to the start of the block you're in, like a media player's back button. At a block's start it goes to the previous block; while playing, press it twice quickly to do that.
- **Alt+Shift+→** goes to the next block after the playhead.
- The previous and next buttons under the video do the same. ↑ ↓ and K J still step through the list from the selected block.

## Project notes for AI help

- Click **Notes** in AI help to tell the AI what the frames can't show: who the characters are and how to tell them apart, where and when it's set, and your team's style. Every draft and message includes them, and they're saved with the project. **Notes ✓** shows when there are some.

## Fixes and improvements

- "Sounds like" words now survive a page reload. The autosave used to leave them out; project files always kept them.
- Long AI help conversations no longer slow down: only the latest messages resend their video frames, which also keeps costs down with online providers.
- Ollama can now run in Docker next to Scribecue, as an optional service (see the README). On a Mac, the Ollama app is faster.

## New address

The web version now lives at **https://scribecue.kyleadvoice.ca**. The old address forwards there. Anything kept in the browser at the old address, such as unsaved work, settings and Piper voices, stays with it: save your work as a project file first, then open it at the new address.

## AI help

A new drawer beside the video helps you describe what's on screen, using your own AI provider. Click **AI** at the top, or press **Alt+Shift+A**.

- **Draft this block:** sends stills from the selected block, the script around it and how many words fit at your voice's speed. The draft appears in the drawer; click **Use for block** to put it in (Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes it), or **Try again**. Nothing changes until you choose.
- **Chat:** ask about the scene, with the frame at the playhead if you like.
- **Providers:** Claude, OpenAI or Gemini with your own API key; OpenRouter by signing in or with a key; or Ollama, which runs the model on your own computer so nothing leaves it.
- Keys stay in your browser. Nothing is sent anywhere until you connect a provider and send a message or ask for a draft. Don't use an online provider for programmes you mustn't share.

Usage is billed by your AI provider, separately from any ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini subscription. See the README for setup.

## Delete blocks from the list

- Each row in the block list now ends in a small ×. It stays faint until you point at the row, then deletes that block with one click, just like the Del key.
- Ctrl/Cmd+Z brings the block back.
- Deleting a block that isn't selected leaves your selection where it is.

## Sounds like: fix how words are said

When a voice says a name or word wrong, you can now tell it how to say it, without changing your text.

- In Write mode with text to speech on, select the word in the text box and press **Alt+Shift+P**, or click **sounds like** next to the block's speed.
- Spell it how it sounds, such as *shiv-AWN* for Siobhan, and click **Hear the block** to check.
- Each block keeps its own list. Words are matched whole and in any case, and longer phrases first.
- The reading, its length, Fit speeds to timings, Update all timings and the exported description track all use the new sound. The list, the timeline and SRT exports keep the words as written.
- Projects and VTT exports keep the list, and Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes a change.

## A quieter scrubber

- The scrubber under the video now stays a thin line, with a slim tick at the playhead, until you point at it.
- Hover over it or drag it and it grows to full size, with the round knob and the time under the pointer.
- The strip keeps its height, so the video and controls never shift.

## Scrubber bar under the video

- A new bar between the video and its controls covers the whole programme. Click anywhere on it to jump there, or drag it to scrub through the video.
- Your blocks show as marks along it, with the selected block highlighted, and hovering shows the time under the pointer.
- It doesn't take keyboard focus, so Space, the arrow keys and every other shortcut keep working as before.

## Piper voices start faster in the web version

- Your chosen Piper voice now loads in the background as soon as text to speech is on, so the first block you hear doesn't wait for it.
- A block you ask to hear now goes ahead of readings being prepared in the background, so it starts sooner.
- Hearing a block during a long job such as **Fit speeds to timings** no longer waits for a fresh copy of the voice to load.

## Faster, steadier Fit speeds to timings

- **Fit speeds to timings** now goes through your script once, block by block, so the progress counts up from the first block to the last instead of starting over with fewer blocks left.
- It needs fewer readings per block, and stops as soon as a block can't get any closer.
- In the web version, Piper voices make up to three readings at once, so fitting and **Update all timings** are about 2.5 times faster on long scripts.

## Test a voice

- A **Test** button next to the voice menu in the text to speech panel reads a short sample line, so you can compare voices without selecting a block.

## Natural voices in the web version

Piper voices now work in the web version at https://kyle95wm.github.io/Scribecue/. In Write mode, open the text to speech panel (Alt+Shift+V), turn text to speech on, and under **Natural voices** pick a voice and click **Download**.

- Four English voices: Lessac and Ryan (US), Alba and Alan (UK). Each is about 63 MB, plus a 33 MB speech engine the first time.
- Voices run in your browser, so your script stays on your computer, and they work offline once downloaded.
- Reading lengths are exact straight away, and you can export a description track, just like Piper with Docker.
- **Remove** frees the space again.

## Fixes

- The web version no longer asks about update checks when you close the welcome setup early. It updates itself.
- The web version no longer looks for a Piper container it doesn't have.

## New: use Scribecue straight from your browser

Scribecue now has a web version, with nothing to install: **https://kyle95wm.github.io/Scribecue/**

- Open it in **Google Chrome** or **Microsoft Edge** and start working.
- Click **Install app** (bottom right), or the install icon in the address bar, to give Scribecue its own window and icon, like any other app. It then works offline.
- It updates itself. When a new version is ready, it asks you to reload, and nothing reloads until you choose to.
- Your video, audio and scripts are still opened straight from your computer and never uploaded. Only the app itself is downloaded, from GitHub, the first time and when it updates.

The web version doesn't include Piper voices yet. For those, or to keep even the app itself on your computer, run Scribecue yourself with Docker, as before.

## New: a notice in other browsers

Scribecue is built for Chrome and Edge. In other browsers, such as Safari and Firefox, it now tells you that some features may not be available, and lists the ones that browser lacks, until you choose **Don't show again**.

## Also

- Scribecue has an app icon.

## How to update

- **Web version:** nothing to do.
- **Docker:** in the Scribecue folder, run `git pull` and then `docker compose up -d --build`, and reload the page. Your text blocks and settings are kept.

## Fixed

- **Closing the text to speech panel during a job** now stops it cleanly and always shows the result on screen, even though the panel has closed. That covers **Fit speeds to timings** and **Update all timings**. **Export description track** keeps running, and shows when it's saved.
- If **Fit speeds to timings** stops before a Piper voice has reached some blocks, those blocks are now left exactly as they were. Before, they could change speed later, the next time you selected or edited them. The message says how many blocks were fitted and how many were left.
- The count of blocks that **can't fit** now only includes blocks whose reading really misses, or whose speed is at its limit.

## How to update

In the Scribecue folder, run `git pull` and then `docker compose up -d --build`, and reload the page. Your text blocks and settings are kept.

## New: choose what happens to an opened script's timings

When you open an SRT or VTT script in Write mode with text to speech on, Scribecue now asks what to do with its timings:

1. **Keep the timings, and fit the reading speeds:** each line speeds up or slows down to fill its block. Best when the timing is already right.
2. **Change the ends to match the readings:** each block ends where its reading finishes, never running into the next block.
3. **Leave everything as it is:** lines that don't fit show their duration in red.

The first two open the text to speech panel so you can watch the progress, and one Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes the change. Tick **Always do this** to stop being asked, and change your choice later under **When you open a script** in the text to speech panel. Opening a Scribecue project doesn't ask, and neither does Transcribe mode.

## New: a tip about Piper

If you haven't added Piper, the text to speech panel now ends with a short **Did you know?** box. It explains what Piper's natural-sounding voices add and how to turn them on.

## How to update

In the Scribecue folder, run `git pull` and then `docker compose up -d --build`, and reload the page. Your text blocks and settings are kept.

## New: Fit speeds to timings

A new button in the text to speech panel does the opposite of **Update all timings**. Every block keeps its timing, and its reading speeds up or slows down to fill it, between −50% and +100%. It's made for scripts whose timing is already right, such as one opened from an SRT or VTT file.

- Blocks with a speed you picked yourself keep it.
- It asks first, shows its progress with a Stop button, and one Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes it. Afterwards it tells you how many blocks couldn't fit within the limits.
- With a Piper voice the fit is exact, and blocks keep fitting as you edit their text or resize them.

## Changed

- **New** is now the first button at the top. As well as clearing every block, it closes the video. It always asks first, naming what will be cleared.

## Fixed

- Fitting a block's speed to its length, after resizing it, now lands exactly with Piper voices. Before, it fell slightly short and could keep shifting when you selected the block, because a reading's length doesn't change evenly with speed.

## How to update

In the Scribecue folder, run `git pull` and then `docker compose up -d --build`, and reload the page. Your text blocks and settings are kept.

## New: resizing a block changes its reading speed

In Write mode with text to speech on, change a block's length and its reading now speeds up or slows down to fill the new length exactly. This works whether you drag an edge, use A, S, Q, W, E or R, or type a time in IN or OUT.

- The block's speed shows as **custom**, such as **custom (−12%)**, in its speed menu, in the list and on the timeline.
- It keeps fitting as you edit the text, and stays between −50% and +100%. If a line can't fit even at +100%, the timing check stays red.
- A speed you pick yourself, from the block's menu or with **[** and **]**, is kept when you resize the block. Set it back to default and resizing fits it again.
- Turn this off with **Change a block's reading speed when you resize it** in the text to speech panel.

## New: notes in [square brackets]

If your team writes notes in the script inside square brackets, such as `[Wide shot, hold for the door]`, tick **Don't read notes in [square brackets]** in the text to speech panel. The notes are then left out of every reading, reading time and auto end, and out of the exported description track, but stay in the script and in SRT and VTT exports. It's off by default.

## How to update

In the Scribecue folder, run `git pull` and then `docker compose up -d --build`, and reload the page. Your text blocks and settings are kept.

## New: project files

Keep each piece of work as a **Scribecue project** (`.scribecue`), and switch between projects whenever you like. A project keeps everything: the blocks, each block's text to speech speed and whether its end follows the reading, the mode and its settings, where you were, and which video it belongs to.

- **Ctrl/Cmd+S** saves the project. The first time, Scribecue asks where. After that it saves straight back to the same file, even after a reload. **Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+S** saves a copy under a new name. Saving in place needs Chrome or Edge; other browsers download a copy each time.
- **Ctrl/Cmd+O** opens a project, or an SRT or VTT script. You can also drop it on the window.
- After opening a project, Scribecue tells you which video to open, warns you if you pick a different one, and puts the playhead back where you left it.
- A dot after the project name at the top means there are unsaved changes. Opening something over unsaved work asks first.
- **New** replaces Clear: it starts a fresh project, asks first, and can be undone.

### Changed keys

Exporting has moved, since **Ctrl/Cmd+S** now saves the project:

- **Ctrl/Cmd+E** exports SRT, and **Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+E** exports WebVTT.

Exports are for the finished script, or for handing it to someone who doesn't use Scribecue, such as another writer or a QC reviewer.

## New: update alert

If you check for updates, a new version now brings down an alert at the top of the window, with the steps to update and a link to what's new. **Later** hides it until you next open Scribecue; **Skip this version** hides it until a newer one comes out.

## How to update

In the Scribecue folder, run `git pull` and then `docker compose up -d --build`, and reload the page. Your text blocks and settings are kept.

## New: welcome setup

A short setup now helps new users get going. It opens the first time you use Scribecue, and the new **Setup** button at the top runs it again at any time.

1. **Welcome:** what Scribecue is, and that your files stay on your computer.
2. **Your task:** transcribing existing audio description, or writing new audio description.
3. **The tools for it:** the hold-to-mark reaction offset for transcribing, or text to speech for writing, with its voice (Piper voices included, if you've added Piper), speed, reading while playing and block ends set from the reading.
4. **Update checks:** once a day, or never.
5. **Done:** a summary of your choices and the keys to start with.

Nothing changes until you press **Finish**, so skipping leaves everything as it was. When you run it again, it starts from your current settings.

If you already use Scribecue, the setup won't open by itself: Setup at the top is there whenever you want it.

## How to update

In the Scribecue folder, run `git pull` and then `docker compose up -d --build`, and reload the page. Your text blocks and settings are kept.

## Changed

- **Update all timings** now shows a progress bar in place of its button while it runs, with the count and a Stop button beside it. **Export description track** shows one too, with the count. The buttons come back when the job finishes.

## How to update

In the Scribecue folder, run `git pull` and then `docker compose up -d --build`, and reload the page. Your text blocks and settings are kept.

## New: Piper voices, exact timings and description track export

Scribecue can now use [Piper](https://github.com/OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl), an open-source speech engine with natural-sounding voices, running in a second container next to the editor. Its voices run on your computer and work offline, so your script never leaves it. Piper is optional: Scribecue works as before without it.

With a Piper voice, in Write mode:

- **Lengths are exact straight away.** A block's reading time is exact as soon as it has text, and **Update all timings** uses the real readings in a second or two, with no silent read-through.
- **Each line always takes the same time,** so the timing you see is the timing you get, between sessions and in the export.
- **Export description track** saves every block's reading as one WAV file, each starting at its block's start time and as long as the video, ready to mix with the programme. It tells you if any readings overlap.

Four English voices are included: Lessac and Ryan (US), and Alba and Alan (UK). You can choose others from the Piper voice list.

### Setting it up

Create a file called `.env` in the Scribecue folder containing `COMPOSE_PROFILES=piper`, then run `docker compose up -d --build`. The first build downloads Piper and its voices, about 1 GB. After that the Piper container has no internet access, and only Scribecue's own server can reach it. See the README for details.

## How to update

In the Scribecue folder, run `git pull` and then `docker compose up -d --build`, and reload the page. Your text blocks and settings are kept. To add Piper at the same time, create the `.env` file first.

Scribecue is now focused on audio description, so this release removes features that only made sense for subtitles, or that weren't being used.

## Removed

- **Reading speed (CPS):** the list column, the figure in the block editor, the I key and the CPS button under the video. In Write mode, the text to speech reading time shows whether a line fits.
- **Line length and line count warnings**, which are on-screen subtitle conventions.
- **Snapping:** dragging no longer sticks block edges to the playhead or neighbouring blocks, and hold-to-mark no longer moves edges to the waveform. The B key and the SNAP button are gone. Hold-to-mark still applies its reaction offset.

Your saved settings for these are cleared automatically.

## Changed

- **Open subs** is now **Open script**. Scripts still open and save as SRT or WebVTT files.
- The block list has more room for text now that the CPS column is gone.
- The README leads with transcribing and writing audio description, and has new screenshots.

## How to update

## New: Transcribe and Write modes

A switch next to the Scribecue name lets you pick what you're doing, and shows only the features for it.

- **Transcribe**, for existing audio description at its original timing: hold-to-mark (H) and its reaction offset (Shift+H).
- **Write**, for new audio description: text to speech, reading times, block speeds, block ends set from the reading, and Update all timings.
- Looping, snapping, audio tracks, reading speed (CPS) and the player controls are in both.

Switching only hides features: block speeds and settings are kept for when you switch back. Pressing a key from the other mode tells you which mode it's in, and the shortcuts overlay (?) lists only the keys for the current mode. Scribecue remembers your choice. If you'd already turned text to speech on, it starts in Write.

## New: block ends set from the reading

With text to speech on, a new block you create with **↵** or **N** now takes its end from how long the voice takes to read it, at the voice and speed you've chosen.

- The end follows the reading as you type, and when you change the block's speed, the overall speed or the voice. Once the block has been read aloud, the exact length replaces the estimate.
- An **auto** tag next to OUT shows which blocks do this.
- The end never runs into the next block. If the line doesn't fit, it stops there and the timing check turns red.
- Set the end yourself, by dragging it, pressing S, E or R, or typing in OUT, and the block keeps it from then on.
- Blocks marked with H, drawn on the timeline or opened from a file keep their timing.
- You can turn this off in the text to speech panel (⌥⇧V).

## New: text to speech

Hear your audio description lines read aloud, to check where each one sits and whether it fits before the next piece of dialogue. It's off until you turn it on: press **⌥⇧V** (Alt+Shift+V on Windows and Linux), or click **TTS** under the video.

- **V** reads the block from its start with the video playing. Playback stops at the block's end, or where the reading ends if it runs over, and tells you whether the line fits.
- **⇧V** reads the block, then sets its end to where the reading finishes.
- **Read blocks aloud while playing**, with the original audio turned down while each block is read.
- **Speeds** from very slow (−30%) to experimental (+100%). The voice also follows the playback speed.
- **Timing check:** the editor shows how long the reading takes, in red if it's longer than the block.

Scribecue uses the voices built into your computer, so your script stays on it. **Online voices** are a separate opt-in: they often sound more natural, but each block's text is sent to the company that runs the voice, such as Google or Microsoft.

Text to speech is for checking timing. It doesn't create an audio file.

First release of Scribecue, a keyboard-first subtitle and audio description editor that runs locally in Docker.

- Frazier-style keyboard layout, waveform timeline streamed from disk, audio track picker
- Hold-to-mark (H) with reaction offset and waveform snapping, block looping (L)
- SRT and VTT import and export, autosave in the browser
- Opt-in daily update check against GitHub releases
